prompt: Strip HTML tags with a RELUCTANT quantifier (a greedy one would swallow the whole line) and collapse accidentally doubled words using a back-reference in both the pattern and the replacement.
explanation: A quantifier followed by ? is reluctant: .*? takes as little as possible, so <.*?> stops at the first '>' and matches one tag instead of running from the first '<' to the last '>'. A back-reference \1 inside a pattern re-matches the exact text that group 1 captured, which is how a repeated word is recognised without knowing the word in advance, and $1 in the replacement puts that single copy back. The \b word boundaries stop the pattern from matching a partial word, and because replaceAll continues scanning after the text it just replaced, a triple repeat is only collapsed once.
hints: stripTags is a one-line replaceAll; the only subtlety is the ? after .* that makes the quantifier reluctant.
In a Java string the back-reference is written "\\1" and the word class is "\\w+".
The replacement string "$1" inserts the captured word, which leaves exactly one copy behind.
